title: The Dripping Tap
intro: A quiet kitchen. One persistent drip. Explore a model tap, spot the likely cause, and learn why checking the water supply comes first.
takeaway: Different taps use different parts. Find the manufacturer's instructions and ask a qualified plumber when isolation, damage, or the repair is uncertain.

steps.title: Follow the drip
steps.prompt: The handle is off, but water falls from the spout. Which fixture needs attention?
steps.hint: Look at the blue droplets beneath the curved spout.
steps.explanation: The drip comes from the tap's spout. Observing where water appears is more useful than guessing at an unseen pipe.

steps.title: Look beneath the symptom
steps.prompt: In this model washer tap, what is a likely reason water still passes when it is closed?
choices: A worn internal washer or seal
steps.hint: A tap needs a watertight seal to stop the flow.
steps.explanation: A worn washer or seal can let water through. This is a learning model: ceramic cartridge taps and other designs use different components.

steps.title: Build a gentle toolkit
steps.prompt: Which tool can gently turn a suitable tap fitting while a cloth protects its finish?
steps.hint: Choose a tool that fits the flat sides without striking or cutting.
steps.explanation: A correctly fitted spanner can turn a suitable fitting. Protect the finish, follow the manufacturer's guidance, and never force seized parts.

steps.title: Put safety in sequence
steps.prompt: Build the model maintenance sequence. Choose the next tile.
puzzle: Open the tap to verify flow has stopped
In the model, replace the matching worn washer
steps.hint: Stop the supply before touching internal parts; then verify isolation.
steps.explanation: Isolation comes before opening a fitting. If water does not stop, stop the task and get help. This simulation does not authorize work on a real tap.

steps.title: Know when to stop
steps.prompt: You cannot confidently identify or isolate the water supply. What is the best next step?
choices: Stop and ask a qualified plumber
Cover the drip and ignore it forever
steps.hint: Uncertainty about isolation is a reason to stop.
steps.explanation: Knowing your limits is a practical skill. A qualified plumber can identify the tap type, isolate it safely, and check the actual fault.

title: The Slow Sink
intro: The bathroom sink is taking its time. Investigate common causes and practise a gentle first-response sequence without harsh chemicals.
takeaway: Use a drain screen and dispose of debris in the bin. Recurring clogs, leaks, multiple blocked drains, or standing chemical cleaner call for professional help.

steps.title: Read the room
steps.prompt: Water lingers in the basin, but the tap shuts off normally. What are you investigating?
steps.hint: Watch the water collected around the drain.
steps.explanation: The symptom is slow drainage. It does not by itself prove where a blockage is, so begin with simple, visible observations.

steps.title: Find a likely cause
steps.prompt: What commonly collects near a bathroom sink stopper?
steps.hint: Think about what gets washed off during everyday bathroom use.
steps.explanation: Hair and soap residue can restrict flow around the stopper. A recurring problem may have a different cause and deserves professional inspection.

steps.title: Choose a safe first response
steps.prompt: No drain cleaner has been used. Which is the gentlest first inspection?
choices: Pour boiling water into an unknown basin
With gloves, inspect visible stopper debris
steps.hint: Start with visible, accessible debris. Avoid chemicals and excessive heat.
steps.explanation: Inspect accessible debris with gloves and follow the stopper's instructions. Never mix cleaners. If cleaner is already present, do not reach into or plunge it; seek advice.

steps.title: Restore the flow
steps.prompt: Put the gentle inspection sequence in order. Choose the next tile.
puzzle: Check that no drain cleaner is present
Remove only accessible debris with gloves
Test with a small amount of lukewarm water
steps.hint: Check for chemicals first, inspect accessible debris second, and test last.
steps.explanation: Check, clear accessible debris, then test gently. Stop if water backs up, a leak appears, or parts resist. Do not dismantle hidden pipework in this exercise.

steps.title: Keep it flowing
steps.prompt: Which habit helps prevent another hair-and-soap blockage?
choices: Use a drain screen and bin collected hair
Wash more hair down the drain
steps.hint: Catch debris before it travels into the pipe.
steps.explanation: A drain screen catches hair for disposal in the bin. Persistent slow drainage or several affected fixtures should be assessed by a qualified plumber.

title: The Sticking Door
intro: An interior door catches at the frame. Read the clues, inspect the hinges, and align a virtual door with a few careful remote-control moves.
takeaway: Swelling, a shifting frame, or hardware can all cause sticking. This model uses a loose hinge. Fire doors, heavy doors, cracks, and persistent problems need qualified help.

steps.title: Notice the clue
steps.prompt: The model door rubs near its upper edge. What should you observe first?
choices: The gap around the door and hinge condition
steps.hint: Compare the gap on each side and look at the hinge leaves.
steps.explanation: The gaps and hinges offer useful clues. Swelling, a loose hinge, and movement in the frame can look similar, so observation comes before adjustment.

steps.title: Choose an inspection
steps.prompt: Which first check is appropriate for this lightweight, ordinary interior-door model?
choices: Check whether a visible hinge screw is loose
Slam the door until it closes
steps.hint: Choose a small, visible check that leaves the door supported.
steps.explanation: Look for a visibly loose screw while leaving the door supported. Never remove all hinges or put fingers in the hinge gap. Real heavy doors need appropriate assistance.

steps.title: Pick the fitting tool
steps.prompt: Which tool fits a cross-head hinge screw in our model?
steps.hint: Match the shape and size of the screw head.
steps.explanation: A matching screwdriver reduces slipping and damage. Do not overtighten or keep turning a stripped screw. Follow the hardware manufacturer's guidance.

steps.title: Align the virtual door
steps.prompt: The teal marker shows the door's alignment. Use the adjustment buttons to place it in the amber target, then check.
steps.hint: Move the marker until its value is zero. This only adjusts the illustration.
steps.explanation: The model's even gap represents alignment. Real doors can stick for several reasons; do not plane, alter, or adjust a fire door based on this simulation.

steps.title: Recognise a bigger problem
steps.prompt: The door keeps sticking and new cracks appear around the frame. What should you do?
choices: Stop and seek a qualified assessment
steps.hint: A changing frame or new cracks need an assessment beyond hinge adjustment.
steps.explanation: Persistent sticking with new cracks may involve the frame or building. Stop forcing the door and contact the property owner or a qualified professional.
